title: Canopy inference elevator cards (iter0)
content:
Purpose and audience: compact, skimmable "Canopy" card set for SEs and platform sellers to use in short calls (3–8 minutes) with integration architects and platform teams. Focus: resilience, fallback economics, and realistic pilot gating criteria. Not a full deck — quick-cards + one-page scripts + 2 mini-scenarios + checklist.

How to use this doc: pull 2–3 cards into a shared Google Slide during a buyer call, then use the scripts below. These are intentionally terse; use them as voice prompts not read-aloud text.

Card index (8 short cards)
1) Quick value (15s) — "Predictable inference economics + resilient fallbacks. Run the same API in hosted, dedicated, or private modes with observability to measure unit cost impacts in 48 hours."
2) Latency-First pitch (30s) — "We route by policy: sub-100ms tail with dedicated pools, can fall back to cost-optimized variants when load spikes to preserve availability."
3) Cost-control hook (30s) — "Optimize with automatic batching + prefix/KV caching; our Optimize engine recommends quantization/profile changes based on token distribution."
4) Security/Compliance (20s) — "Private deployments: VPC control plane, KMS integration, audit logs; we support on-prem air-gapped rollouts for regulated data."
5) Fallback economics (45s) — "If dedicated capacity saturates, Canopy fallbacks to compatible smaller variants in the same model family — keep UX online while reducing cost by ~2–5x depending on workload."
6) Observability hook (20s) — "Per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, and alerting tied to prompt set regressions — enable early rollback before user-visible errors."
7) Pilot success criteria (quick) — "2k daily inference units, <150ms p95 latency in steady state, correct fallbacks in chaos test, measurable cost/unit reduction >15% after Optimize tuning."
8) Migration safety net (quick) — "Canary + automatic rollback + traffic shadowing built into rollouts; platform team maintains pinning to exact model versions."

Script snippets (what to say)
- Opening (30s): "We help platform teams get consistent inference economics — same API, same controls, different runtime choices. For your latency-sensitive flows we recommend starting in dedicated mode for predictable p95, then introduce Optimize to reduce spend as you learn token shapes."
- Objection: 'We already have GPUs on-prem' (20s): "Great — many customers keep a hybrid: run burst/dedicated in-cloud for peak and pin sensitive workloads on-prem. We provide the same routing and observability so your SREs can treat both uniformly."
- Objection: 'Risk of model drift when fallbacking' (25s): "We surface QA/regression scores for each fallback variant and let you bind prompt test suites to rollout policies; automatic regression alerts stop rollouts if quality drops."

Mini-scenario A: Holiday spike (ops-focused)
- Context: ecommerce search ranking with embedding + reranker; baseline dedicated pool sized for steady 300 qps but traffic triples for promotions.
- Card to use: Fallback economics + Latency-first + Observability
- Scriptable pitch: "During spikes we keep the endpoint online by routing overflow to a smaller compatible variant for non-critical traffic and to regional burst capacity for critical checkout calls. We instrumented a customer where this reduced outage risk from 12% to <1% during promo peaks."
- Quick config notes for SEs: add route rules: {priority: checkout, model: high-tier, fallback: regional-burst}; set canary to 10% for promo traffic; enable prefix caching for repeated query expansions.

Mini-scenario B: Confidential document processing for a regulated customer (security-focused)
- Context: client needs private deployment inside VPC; initial pilot is 10k docs/month with heavy context sizes; team worried about audit surface and KMS.
- Card to use: Security/Compliance + Pilot success criteria + Migration safety net
- Script: "We can run a private control plane in your VPC with HSM-backed keys, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. Start with a canary ingest for 10% of traffic into an on-prem pool; we shadow responses to hosted service for regression checks before turning on live traffic."
- Quick config notes: require data residency in region, enable audit-forwarding to project SIEM, integrate customer KMS alias during provisioning (Jira: GTMP-942 notes).

Cheat checklist for pilot kickoff (one-pager)
- Pre-kickoff: confirm SSO/KMS contacts, order dedicated pool estimate (approx GPU-days), define prompt test suite (3–5 golden prompts).
- Day 0–2: provision resources, run synthetic load test to validate autoscale, enable tracing hooks.
- Day 3–7: run 50% shadow traffic, evaluate token distribution and Optimize suggestions, tune batching window.
- Day 8–14: roll canary to 10–25% live traffic, verify fallback economics under 1.5x load, run chaos test (drop 20% capacity) to assert fallbacks.
- Success gate: p95 < target, fallback correctness > 98% on test prompts, cost per inference trending down after Optimize recommendations.

Quick technical reference (for SEs to paste into Slack)
- Example API call (pseudo): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-3b", "input":"...", "route":"platform-checkout" }' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Observability links to pull: Console -> Routes -> <route> -> Token cost breakdown; use trace-id returned in response for cross-correlation.
- Common knobs: batching_window_ms, kv_cache_enabled (true/false), quant_profile (recommended: q8_0, q4_1 for embed-heavy).

Playbook snippets (what to put in a follow-up email post-demo)
- Subject: Quick pilot next steps & 3 checkboxes
- Body bullet points: provision estimate / confirm SSO & KMS / provide 3 golden prompts for regression tests. Attach: pilot-checklist.docx, sample trace output, service-level draft.

Open questions / items to refine (sprint items for cardset iteration)
- Add a microcard focused on embedding-heavy use cases (semantic search) with sample unit-economics numbers per 1M tokens.
- We need a condensed 'ops playbook' card for SREs that includes exact autoscale defaults and a short rollback script.
- Create a one-slide visual showing routing decision tree (latency-first vs cost-first) for quick use in live demos.

References (internal)
- Confluence playbook: INF-PLAYBOOK-183 (contains full rollout patterns)
- Jira: GTMP-942 (pilot config for KMS onboarding)
- GitHub PR: repo/redwood-playbooks/pull/87 (sample automation snippets)

Notes to self (informal)
- This is intentionally terse; field SEs want 3–4 cards max per call. Keep language low-ceremony.
- Follow up with design team to make 1-slide visual (due next sprint).
- Ask research for concrete numbers on fallback cost multipliers for 2/4/8k sequence lengths.

Last edited by Asha Patel — jot down a test-run with Liam 11/18 before wider playbook adoption.
